results.title: Colombia vs DR Congo World Cup 2026: Preview, Prediction & Analysis
highlights:
Colombia vs DR Congo World Cup 2026
[...]
Colombia vs DR Congo at the FIFA World Cup 2026 is a Group K clash that could shape who advances from one of the tournament’s most intriguing groups. The two sides meet on June 23 at Estadio Guadalajara (Estadio Akron) in Zapopan, Mexico, with kick-off at 10:00 PM ET. Both teams will be desperate for points in a group that also includes Portugal and Uzbekistan.
[...]
Colombia enter the match ranked 13th in the world, comfortably ahead of DR Congo in 46th. The Cafeteros are coming off two pre-tournament losses to France and Croatia, though they showed plenty of attacking quality in wins over Australia and New Zealand. The Leopards arrive on the back of a stunning qualifier run that ended a 52-year absence from the World Cup stage.
[...]
This match matters far beyond three points. For Colombia, it is a must-win on paper against the group’s lowest-ranked side. For DR Congo, a result here would be an enormous statement and give them a genuine shot at the group stage knockout round.
[...]

[...]

[...]
| WC Record (W-D-L) | 9-2-11 | 0-0-3 |
| Manager | Néstor Lorenzo | Sébastien Desabre |
[...]
Colombia vs DR Congo World Cup 2026 is a match that looks like a comfortable Colombia win on paper. But DR Congo are not the Zaire side of 1974. They are a team with Premier League and Ligue 1 quality throughout the squad, a coach who prepares meticulously, and a momentum that comes from beating Nigeria and Cameroon on the way here.
[...]
The X-factor is the counter-attack. If Wissa gets one or two real opportunities against Colombia’s high defensive line, he has the quality to score. Colombia will likely dominate possession and create more chances. Whether they convert enough of them is the real question. Lorenzo’s side has scored freely in the pre-tournament warmups, but France and Croatia both showed they can be hurt when opponents press back. The full match schedule shows Colombia already face Uzbekistan before this game, so their form and confidence heading into June 23 will matter greatly.
[...]
Colombia have the quality, the depth, and the World Cup experience to win this match. Díaz and Rodríguez should be the difference. But expect DR Congo to make it hard, compete for long stretches, and perhaps create a genuine scare before Colombia’s class tells in the final quarter of the game.
[...]
Our Prediction: Colombia 2-0 DR Congo
[...]
Colombia win it through a Díaz goal and a set-piece. DR Congo defend well for large parts but cannot cope with the quality in Colombia’s final third. A clean sheet for the Cafeteros as their defensive structure holds firm against Wissa and Bakambu.
